bull.b: The large recurring revenue base from instruments, accessories, and service ties financial performance to procedures and the installed system base. This creates visibility beyond one-time system sales and supports durable monetization as utilization expands across hospitals and specialties.

A growing installed base strengthens Intuitive’s market position because each additional system can generate future procedures, consumables demand, and service revenue. Expansion also broadens the company’s clinical footprint and provides a platform for adoption of newer robotic offerings.

bull.t: Profitability, cash flow, and balance sheet
bull.b: Strong cash generation and exceptionally low leverage provide financial resilience and flexibility to fund research, commercial expansion, and customer support internally. High margins and solid cash conversion also make the business less dependent on financing conditions while supporting sustained investment.

bear.t: Growth moderation and U.S. coverage pressure
bear.b: Slower U.S. procedure growth could temper the pace of recurring instrument revenue and system utilization, especially because the domestic market is a major adoption base. Coverage changes and deferred benign procedures may also make near-term demand less predictable.

China’s weaker tenders, domestic competition, and policy-driven pricing pressure constrain system placements and may limit revenue growth in an important international market. The lack of da Vinci 5 clearance there further restricts the near-term product mix and adoption opportunity.

bear.t: Extended-use instruments may reduce recurring revenue per procedure
bear.b: If extended-use instruments are adopted broadly, customers may purchase fewer replacement instruments for some benign procedures. That could reduce instrument-and-accessory revenue per procedure and weaken the recurring economics of the razor-and-blades model even if procedure volumes continue growing.
